diagnostic_evidence.quote: A map $A_\omega \colon \Omega \times \Omega \to \Omega$ is called a binary average (or, for short, average) in $X$ if it satisfies:

issues.failure_explanation: The expression is an argmin and may be set-valued. In a two-point metric space with d=1 and omega=1/2, both points minimize the functional, so no single-valued map A_omega:Omega x Omega -> Omega is defined unless a selection is specified.

failure_location.quote: It is easy to verify that if the metric $d$ is continuous as a function of its arguments, then the binary Fr\'echet mean satisfies all the requirements of Definition~\ref{def:average}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the example to spaces where the binary Frechet mean is unique and continuous in omega, or specify a consistent selection.
issues.overall_effect: The Frechet mean example does not establish a valid average in an arbitrary complete metric space.
issues.title: Frechet mean example is not well-defined as an average in general CMS
issues.why_classification: A local restriction or selection fixes the example without affecting the main convergence or proximity theorems.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (End points interpolation) For any $x,y \in \Omega$, $A_0(x,y) = x$ and $A_1(x,y) = y$.

issues.failure_explanation: As written, A_0(A,B) is the set of b with (a,b) in Pi, i.e. B, while A_1(A,B) is A. This contradicts the endpoint interpolation requirement and also reverses the metric property.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed intrinsic average for compact sets is not an average as defined; the example is unsupported until the formula is corrected.
issues.title: Compact-sets average has reversed endpoints
issues.why_classification: A one-line coefficient swap restores the stated example and preserves the intended application.

issues.failure_explanation: An optimal plan gamma minimizing J_p need not be unique. Different optimal plans can give different pushforwards under pi_omega, so the proposed average is not well-defined as a map without a selection or a uniqueness assumption.

failure_location.quote: Specifically, when $\gamma$ of~\eqref{eqn:joint_measures} is obtained, the average between $\mu_{0}$ and $\mu_{1}$ is given by the pushforward,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume uniqueness of the optimal plan/geodesic or specify a continuous selection of optimal plans before defining the average.
issues.overall_effect: The Wasserstein-space example does not define a valid average in full generality.
issues.title: Wasserstein average may be nonunique
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard uniqueness/selection condition fixes the illustrative example without changing the main theorems.

issues.failure_explanation: The Bezier curve tangent is generally a non-unit vector. The second component of an element of Omega must lie in the unit sphere S^{n-1}, so the pair is not in Omega unless the tangent direction is normalized.

failure_location.quote: Finally, we define the average ${\mathcal A}_{\omega}$ as the pair consisting of the value of the B\'ezier curve at $t=\omega$ and the tangent of the  B\'ezier curve there.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the second component as the normalized tangent direction of the Bezier curve at t=omega.
issues.overall_effect: The stated geometric Hermite average is not a map into the declared space as written.
issues.title: Hermite Bezier average may output non-unit tangent
issues.why_classification: Normalization is a local correction that preserves the intended Hermite average example.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Next, we show by induction that for any $k$, $S^k(\PP)_{2^{k}j+r}$, $r=0,\ldots,2^{k}-1$ is independent of $\PP_\ell$ for
Finally, by~\eqref{eqn:induction_proof2}, we obtain a uniform locality range of $2M_S$, for all $S^k$, $k \in \N$.

issues.failure_explanation: For S^{k+1}(P)_{2^{k+1}j+tilde r}, the level-k indices involved are around 2^k j, not 2j. The displayed induction hypothesis with 2j does not imply the desired bound for k>1, so the proof of the claimed locality range is invalid as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the induction to use the parent index 2^k j+floor(tilde r/2) and complete the standard locality estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The stated locality lemma is not established by the given proof.
issues.title: Locality lemma induction uses wrong index scale
issues.why_classification: The lemma statement is standard and can be proved by a corrected local indexing argument; no substantive conclusion is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem allows arbitrary initial parameters t^0_j, but the elementary scheme is described with the primal parameterization t_i^k=i2^{-k}. The proof compares Gamma(t_i^0) to the limit at t_i^0 using p^0_j=p^k_{2^k j}, which requires t^k_{2^k j}=t^0_j and compatible nested intervals; this is not assumed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the assumption that the parameter refinement is the primal/midpoint refinement with t^k_{2^k j}=t^0_j, or restrict T^0 to uniformly spaced parameters with gap h.
issues.overall_effect: The O(h) approximation statement is unsupported for general initial parameterizations as written.
issues.title: Approximation theorem assumes unstated parameter nesting
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard parameter-nesting hypothesis preserves the intended approximation result.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes decay only for multiples of L: delta(W^{kL}P). For L>1 it does not bound delta(W^r(W^{kL}P)) for 0<r<L, so the small-delta set need not be invariant under all iterates. Theorem 4.2 therefore cannot be applied from the stated density condition alone.

failure_location.quote: Finally, the weak convergence of the scheme $W$ follows by Theorem~\ref{thm:convergence} since $W$ has a contractivity factor when $\delta(\PP)$ is small enough, it is D-S in $\D$, and it maps $\D$ onto itself.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a hypothesis that the set {P in D: delta(P)<nu} is invariant under W^r for 0<=r<L, or prove such an invariance/boundedness estimate; alternatively restrict the theorem to L=1.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised weak convergence from sufficiently dense initial data is not established for general contractivity number L.
issues.title: First-type proximity theorem lacks intermediate invariance for L>1
issues.why_classification: The repair requires an extra nontrivial invariance condition or a restriction of L; the theorem's general advertised guarantee is weakened, but a comparable result remains possible.

issues.failure_explanation: The index 2i-1 is produced using alpha_{i-1} and v_i-v_{i-1}, not alpha_i and v_i-v_{i+1}. The displayed ± estimate and the conclusion using ||p_{i+1}-p_i|| are therefore not valid for the left neighbor as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat the left case separately with i replaced by i-1, using alpha_{i-1} and ||p_i-p_{i-1}||.
issues.overall_effect: The proof that W maps the Hermite data set D into D is incomplete.
issues.title: Hermite closeness lemma misindexes left refinement rule
issues.why_classification: A local index correction completes the invariance estimate and preserves the corollary.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated second-type proximity of S1^L to S2^L gives a bound only at block levels jL with rate eta^{j+1}. The proof needs, for every ell>=L, a bound for d(S1^L S1^{ell-L}P, S2^L S1^{ell-L}P) of order eta^{ell-L+1}. For L>1 this is a different, stronger all-offset condition that is not established from the definition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must strengthen the second-type proximity hypothesis to the all-offset bound used in the proof, or prove that bound from the stated condition.
issues.overall_effect: The strong convergence theorem for second-type proximity, and the C1 results depending on it, are not derived from the stated proximity hypothesis.
issues.title: Second-type proximity theorem uses an unstated all-level proximity rate
